title: Opening up brackets
objectives: Expand a single bracket using an area model
Expand a bracket with a negative multiplier or a negative term
Check an expansion by substituting a number

screens.prose: A rectangle is 3 units tall. Its width is $n + 2$: a stretch of unknown length $n$, then 2 more units.
screens.question: Take $n = 5$. What is the area of the whole rectangle?

hints.text: How wide is the rectangle when $n = 5$?
The width is the $n$ stretch plus the 2-unit stretch.
Width $5 + 2 = 7$, so the area is $3 \times 7$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the full width first, then multiply by the height.

byKey.first-only: You found $3 \times 5$ and then added 2. The 2-unit stretch is also 3 tall, so it adds $3 \times 2 = 6$.
byKey.added: You added the lengths. Area is height times width.
byKey.left-only: That is the left part only. The 2-unit stretch on the right adds more area.

explain.text: The width is $5 + 2 = 7$, so the area is $3 \times 7 = 21$. Split it instead: $3 \times 5 = 15$ on the left and $3 \times 2 = 6$ on the right. Both routes give 21.

screens.prose: Imagine sliding $n$ longer or shorter. Some pieces of the rectangle stretch with it; others never change.
screens.question: Tap every piece whose area stays the same, whatever $n$ is.

hints.text: Which column has a width that is a fixed number?
The right-hand column is always 2 wide.
All three pieces in the 2-wide column keep their size.

feedback.correct: The three pieces in the 2-wide column.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Pick the pieces whose width is a fixed number.

byKey.n-part: Those pieces are $n$ wide, so they stretch when $n$ changes.
byKey.one-block: That piece is fixed, and so are the two below it. The rectangle is 3 tall.
byKey.c11: That piece is $n$ wide, so its area changes with $n$.
byKey.c21: That piece is $n$ wide, so its area changes with $n$.
byKey.c31: That piece is $n$ wide, so its area changes with $n$.

explain.text: The 2-wide column holds three pieces of area 2, so it is always $3 \times 2 = 6$. The rest is three strips of width $n$: area $3n$. Every rectangle like this splits into a part that moves with $n$ and a part that does not.

screens.prose: The whole area is 3 lots of $n + 2$. We write it $3(n + 2)$: the bracket says multiply everything inside by 3.
screens.question: Add up the pieces. Which expression gives the same area with no bracket?

options.why: You counted one $n$ strip. The rectangle is 3 tall, so there are three: $3n$.
You counted the 2-wide column as area 2. It is 3 tall, so its area is 6.
You added 3 and 2 and put $n$ after them. Only the left part depends on $n$.

hints.text: Find the area of each colour, then add.
The fixed column is 3 tall and 2 wide.
Strips: $3 \times n = 3n$. Fixed column: $3 \times 2 = 6$.

feedback.correct: $3n$ from the strips and 6 from the fixed column.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply each width by the height 3, then add.

explain.text: You found $3n$ for the strips and 6 for the fixed column, so $3(n + 2) = 3n + 6$. Rewriting a bracket as separate terms is **expanding** it. The 3 multiplied both the $n$ and the 2.

screens.prose: A new rectangle is 4 tall and $n + 5$ wide. Its area is $4(n + 5)$.
screens.question: Place the area of each piece. Leave the rest.

hints.text: Each piece is height times width.
The right piece is 4 tall and 5 wide.
Left: $4 \times n = 4n$. Right: $4 \times 5 = 20$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply each width by the height, 4.

byKey.t9: You added 4 and 5. The piece is 4 by 5, so its area is $4 \times 5 = 20$.
byKey.t5: That is the width of the right piece. It is also 4 tall, so its area is 20.
byKey.t5n: You multiplied $5 \times n$. The left piece is 4 tall, so its area is $4n$.

explain.text: The pieces are $4 \times n = 4n$ and $4 \times 5 = 20$. So $4(n + 5) = 4n + 20$. The 4 reached both terms in the bracket.

screens.prose: Now a term inside the bracket has its own number. This rectangle is 5 tall and $2n + 1$ wide: two $n$ strips and one unit strip.
screens.question: Which is $5(2n + 1)$ expanded?

options.why: You multiplied the $2n$ but not the 1. The 1-wide strip is 5 tall, so its area is 5.
You added 5 and 2. Five times $2n$ is $10n$.
You multiplied only the 1. The two $n$ strips are 5 tall too.

hints.text: Find the area of each strip.
Each $n$ strip is 5 tall and $n$ wide.
Two strips of $5n$ make $10n$. The unit strip is $5 \times 1 = 5$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply every term in the bracket by 5.

explain.text: The two $n$ strips give $5n + 5n = 10n$, and the unit strip gives 5. So $5(2n + 1) = 10n + 5$. The 5 multiplies the 2 in $2n$ as well as the 1.

screens.prose: An area cannot be negative, so here we check with numbers instead. The table gives $-2(n - 4)$ worked out directly for two values of $n$.
screens.question: Which is $-2(n - 4)$ expanded? Check your choice against the table.

options.why: You made $-2 \times -4$ negative. Two negatives multiply to a positive. At $n = 0$ the table says 8, not $-8$.
You multiplied only the $n$. The $-2$ multiplies the $-4$ too.
You dropped the minus on the 2. At $n = 10$ that gives 12, but the table says $-12$.

hints.text: Multiply $-2$ by each term inside: $n$ and $-4$.
Try each option at $n = 0$ first.
$-2 \times n = -2n$ and $-2 \times -4 = +8$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply each term inside by $-2$, signs included.

explain.text: The $-2$ multiplies both terms: $-2n$ and $-2 \times -4 = +8$. At $n = 10$, $-20 + 8 = -12$, matching the table. A table check catches a sign slip at once.

screens.prose: Jo expands $3(n + 2)$ and writes $3n + 2$. Look back at the rectangle.
screens.question: Is Jo right?

options.text: No. The 3 multiplies the 2 as well, giving $3n + 6$
Yes. The 3 only goes with the $n$ next to it
options.why: You let the 3 multiply only the $n$. The rectangle is 3 tall all the way across.
You added 3 and 2 for the second term. The 3 multiplies the 2: $3 \times 2 = 6$.
You added 3 and 2 and put $n$ after them. The 2-wide column does not depend on $n$.

hints.text: Test both sides with a number, say $n = 10$.
How many 2-unit pieces does the rectangle have?
$3(10 + 2) = 36$, but $3 \times 10 + 2 = 32$. The 2 needs multiplying too.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count every piece of the rectangle.

byKey.jo: You agreed with Jo, who multiplied only the $n$. At $n = 10$, $3(n + 2) = 36$ but $3n + 2 = 32$.

explain.text: Jo counted the three $n$ strips but only one of the three 2-unit pieces. The missing two pieces add 4, so Jo is short by 4 for every $n$. The right expansion is $3n + 6$.

screens.prose: Each time, the outside number multiplied every term inside the bracket, signs included: $$a(b + c) = ab + ac$$ This is expanding a bracket.
screens.question: Which is $6(n - 2)$ expanded?

options.why: You multiplied only the $n$. The 6 reaches the $-2$ too.
You lost the minus sign. $6 \times -2 = -12$.
You multiplied only the 2. The 6 reaches the $n$ too.

hints.text: Multiply 6 by each term: $n$ and $-2$.
$6 \times n = 6n$ and $6 \times -2 = -12$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply every term inside by 6, keeping the signs.

explain.text: $6 \times n = 6n$ and $6 \times -2 = -12$, so $6(n - 2) = 6n - 12$. A minus inside the bracket stays a minus after a positive multiplier.

screens.prose: Why does the outside number reach every term? Show that $3(n + 2) = 3n + 6$ without a picture.
screens.question: Put the lines in order.

lines.text: $= n + n + n + 2 + 2 + 2$, adding works in any order

hints.text: What does multiplying by 3 mean?
Three times something is that thing added three times.
Write out three copies of $n + 2$, regroup, then collect.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start from what multiplying by 3 means.

byKey.reorder: Regrouping needs the three copies written out first.
byKey.collect: Collecting like terms is the last step.

explain.text: Three lots of $n + 2$ contain three $n$s and three 2s. That is why the 3 multiplies both terms. Collecting gives $3n + 6$.

screens.prose: A portfolio holds 40 shares of stock A at £$n$ each. It also holds 40 shares of stock B at £6.25 each. Its value in pounds is $40(n + 6.25)$.
screens.question: Which is the value expanded?

options.why: You multiplied only A's price. The 40 shares of B are worth $40 \times 6.25 = 250$.
You added 40 and 6.25. B's price does not depend on $n$.
Check the decimal point: $40 \times 6.25 = 250$, since $4 \times 6.25 = 25$.

hints.text: Value is price times quantity for each stock.
B's piece is 40 shares at £6.25.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply 40 by each price.

explain.text: A's holding is worth $40n$ pounds and B's is $40 \times 6.25 = 250$ pounds. So the portfolio is $40n + 250$. If A trades at £8.10, it is worth $324 + 250 = £574$.

ideas: A number outside a bracket multiplies every term inside: $3(n + 2) = 3n + 6$.
An area model shows why: a 3 by $n + 2$ rectangle splits into a $3n$ piece and a 6 piece.
Signs multiply too: $-2(n - 4) = -2n + 8$. Check an expansion by substituting a number.

formula.name: Expanding a bracket
formula.note: The outside factor reaches every term inside, signs included.

summary.trap: $3(n + 2)$ is not $3n + 2$. The 3 multiplies the 2 as well.

options.why: You multiplied only the $n$. The 5 multiplies the 3 as well.
You added 5 and 3. The 5 multiplies the 3: 15.
You added 5 and 3 and put $n$ after them. The 3 does not depend on $n$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply every term inside by 5.

options.why: You multiplied the $2n$ but not the $-1$.
You added 4 and 2. Four lots of $2n$ make $8n$.
You lost the minus sign. $4 \times -1 = -4$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply every term inside by 4, keeping the signs.
Not quite right. Work out the bracket first, or multiply both terms by 7.

byKey.first-only: You worked out $7 \times 6 + 4$. The 7 multiplies the 4 as well: $42 + 28 = 70$.
byKey.added: You added 7, 6 and 4. The 7 multiplies the bracket.

explain.text: Inside first: $6 + 4 = 10$, then $7 \times 10 = 70$. Expanded: $7n + 28 = 42 + 28 = 70$. Both routes agree.

quiz.prose: This time the outside factor is a letter. Picture a rectangle $n$ tall and $n + 3$ wide.
quiz.question: Which is $n(n + 3)$ expanded?

options.why: You added $n$ to $n$. The piece is $n$ by $n$, so its area is $n \times n = n^2$.
You multiplied only the $n$. The 3-wide piece is $n$ tall, so its area is $3n$.
You wrote $n \times n$ as $n$. A number times itself is its square.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply each term inside by $n$.

explain.text: The $n$ by $n$ piece has area $n^2$, and the $n$ by 3 piece has area $3n$. So $n(n + 3) = n^2 + 3n$.
